extraction.body: The $6.3 billion Binance hack could accelerate a shift in how investors value cryptocurrency companies, putting a greater premium on custody providers and the infrastructure needed to securely hold and protect digital assets. Much of crypto's evolution this year has involved companies moving past their reliance on trading volumes and transaction fees, to focus instead on building the infrastructure connecting digital assets with traditional finance. Last Thursday's breach adds a new dimension, bringing cybersecurity, custody, compliance and balance-sheet resilience into sharper focus. Importantly, the Binance breach was not an indictment of crypto itself, or a case of leadership-driven fraud, as with FTX in late 2022. Instead, Binance's leadership moved quickly to contain the fallout , protect customers and commit the exchange's own resources to cover losses. On Tuesday, Binance CEO Richard Teng told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" that the company has replenished 98% of $6.34 billion in affected assets, and that it is still in the process of purchasing outstanding, more illiquid assets. Management's response, alongside efforts elsewhere in the industry to boost confidence, helped prevent a security breach from escalating into a broader crisis of confidence. For example, Tether, Circle, Ripple and others moved quickly to freeze or restrict access to about $3 billion in stolen assets; Coinbase blocked transfers to compromised wallets and offered Binance direct assistance. The hack could even help shape the next phase of the crypto infrastructure trade. The new winners may not just be the businesses with the most users, volume or assets under custody, but the ones that can also demonstrate they're able to protect those assets under extreme duress. "Which company has the resources to invest in cybersecurity and protect customer funds? For a smaller company, it could be much harder because once these crypto companies become infrastructure plays, providing the well for tokenization … they need to have the compliance and control in place so that a similar hacking will not happen or can be minimized," Owen Lau, senior analyst at ClearStreet, told CNBC. "Larger companies have more resources that could give them some advantage." While institutional investors have increasingly embraced digital assets, broader adoption depends on confidence that those assets can be securely held, accessed and transferred. The Binance breach highlights the importance of that infrastructure, and could increase demand for specialized custodians and platforms with established asset-protection capabilities. Coinbase has operated a dedicated institutional custody business since 2018. Circle entered the custody business this year, after the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted it approval to operate as a trust bank . In the past few years, Ripple and Kraken have also launched custody businesses. Still, smaller players compete in the space as well. Small cap crypto exchange stock Gemini Space Station has offered custody services since 2019. BitGo Holdings , founded in 2013, is one of the earliest players in institutional crypto custody and infrastructure, with a reputation for security and serving major institutions. The shift could also drive consolidation as companies look to buy capabilities, deepen their infrastructure offerings and achieve the scale needed to compete, Lau said. Much of crypto's evolution this year has involved companies moving past their reliance on trading volumes and transaction fees, to focus instead on building the infrastructure connecting digital assets with traditional finance. Last Thursday's breach adds a new dimension, bringing cybersecurity, custody, compliance and balance-sheet resilience into sharper focus.

Importantly, the Binance breach was not an indictment of crypto itself, or a case of leadership-driven fraud, as with FTX in late 2022. Instead, Binance's leadership moved quickly to contain the fallout , protect customers and commit the exchange's own resources to cover losses.

On Tuesday, Binance CEO Richard Teng told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" that the company has replenished 98% of $6.34 billion in affected assets, and that it is still in the process of purchasing outstanding, more illiquid assets.

Management's response, alongside efforts elsewhere in the industry to boost confidence, helped prevent a security breach from escalating into a broader crisis of confidence. For example, Tether, Circle, Ripple and others moved quickly to freeze or restrict access to about $3 billion in stolen assets; Coinbase blocked transfers to compromised wallets and offered Binance direct assistance.

The hack could even help shape the next phase of the crypto infrastructure trade. The new winners may not just be the businesses with the most users, volume or assets under custody, but the ones that can also demonstrate they're able to protect those assets under extreme duress.

"Which company has the resources to invest in cybersecurity and protect customer funds? On November 3, Teng told CNBC that Binance had replenished 98% of the $6.34 billion in affected assets. One day later, in its November 4 update, Binance said about $2.85 billion in digital assets had been frozen or intercepted. The exchange added that the figure remained subject to reconciliation and to swings in market prices. Those two numbers answer different questions, and mixing them up is the most common error in coverage so far. Four items stay unconfirmed. First, the claim that this is the largest theft in digital-asset history. Outlets have used that framing, but no audited ledger backs it. Second, the link to North Korea, which has circulated in reports but lacks independent confirmation in the material we reviewed. Third, the $4.7 billion in net customer withdrawals reported after withdrawals resumed. Fourth, the $6.3 billion loss estimate and the $3 billion frozen estimate, which are unaudited disclosures. Two gaps stand out. The 98% and 95% replenishment figures sit three points apart, which on a $6.34 billion base equals roughly $190 million. And the $2.85 billion frozen figure sits about $150 million below the $3 billion estimate CNBC used. Neither gap looks alarming alone. Together they show that the recovery story is still being written. TRM Labs said the attackers compromised Binance’s signing infrastructure, the machinery that authorizes transactions. That finding explains why the damage crossed so many chains at once. A flaw in one smart contract would hit one network. A compromise of the system that produces valid signatures hits every network the exchange touches. Binance’s initial investigation pointed to a different starting point. It indicated an attacker may have compromised a DevOps engineer’s laptop and then reached a service container used to submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We covered that path in our earlier piece on the reported attack chain behind the $6.3 billion loss . The two accounts fit together. A laptop is the door, the service container is the hallway, and the signing layer is the vault. The Financial Express summarized the speed in its headline, saying the exchange lost about $6 billion in 20 minutes. Speed is the point for custody design. A control that needs a human to notice, decide and act cannot beat a sweep that finishes in the time of a coffee break. Controls have to fire automatically, and they have to live outside any system an attacker already holds. CNBC framed the breach as a turning point for how investors value crypto companies. CNBC also drew a line between this event and the FTX collapse of late 2022. The Binance breach, it argued, was neither an indictment of crypto itself nor a case of leadership-driven fraud. Management moved to contain the fallout and committed company resources to cover losses. That distinction explains why the story reads as an infrastructure trade and not a panic. The thesis runs like this. Winners in the next phase may not be the firms with the most users, the biggest volume or the most assets under custody. They may be the firms that can prove they protect assets under extreme duress. CNBC also cited Morgan Stanley in pointing to the separation of custody from execution as the more consequential structural shift, and it noted that the stress could drive consolidation as companies buy capabilities and chase scale. BusinessDay in Nigeria reached a similar reading from a different market. Its coverage said the breach exposes vulnerabilities in crypto custody , which suggests the message is travelling well beyond US trading desks. For emerging markets that lean heavily on exchanges as the entry point to crypto, the lesson lands harder, because few local alternatives exist. My read is that the market is repricing one specific risk: the operational path between a key and a transaction. Holding assets used to mean guarding private keys. After October 29, it means guarding the software, the people and the approval policies that decide when a key may sign. The industry response showed how much of crypto’s safety net sits with a few centralized actors. Tether, Circle, Ripple and other entities moved to freeze or restrict access to roughly $3 billion in stolen assets, according to CNBC. Reports put Tether’s share at nearly $1.57 billion and Circle’s at more than $800 million. Those two firms alone account for about $2.37 billion, which is close to 80% of the $3 billion estimate. Coinbase blocked transfers to compromised wallets and offered Binance direct assistance. Binance said it worked with crypto custodian BitGo to freeze some of the stolen funds. Both details matter for the custody trade, because they show custody firms acting as active defenders in an incident, not merely as vaults waiting for deposits. Names also spread quickly on social media during the first days. We tracked which companies were said to be exposed and found that, as of our earlier reporting, three firms were named but none was confirmed hit . That caution still applies. It echoes the argument for layered custody, where no single failure empties the vault. Limit standing access, isolate build and deploy tooling from finance systems and review who can reach service containers that touch wallets. The $2.85 billion that Binance reported frozen or intercepted came from fast coordination with issuers, custodians and other exchanges. Firms that already have named contacts at stablecoin issuers and custody providers act in minutes. Firms that start a call list mid-incident lose the window. Write the playbook, test it and keep the contacts current. Regulators will watch the same points. Our report on security coverage across ransomware, breaches and compliance shows how often the same operational gaps recur across sectors, from crypto to retail systems. Custody is one more place where basic controls decide the outcome. Binance reported a security incident on October 29, 2026, involving unauthorized withdrawals from hot wallets. Much of crypto’s progress this year, the outlet noted, has come from firms moving beyond reliance on trading volume and fees toward infrastructure that links digital assets to traditional finance.
The Binance incident adds cybersecurity, custody, compliance and balance-sheet resilience to that list of things investors now price.
Binance experienced a security incident on October 29, 2026, involving unauthorized withdrawals from hot wallets.
That spread matters, and we return to it below.
Binance said it worked with crypto custodian BitGo to freeze some of the stolen funds.
Both details matter for the custody trade, because they show custody firms acting as active defenders in an incident, not merely as vaults waiting for deposits.
In the same interview, Zhao said: “When you run a platform, especially a crypto platform, the possibility is always there.” That framing treats breach risk as a permanent operating cost.
The Binance event, as CNBC stressed, did not.
For custody buyers, the difference is large: fraud is a governance question, while a signing-layer breach is an engineering question that better controls can narrow.
Its coverage said the breach exposes vulnerabilities in crypto custody , which suggests the message is travelling well beyond US trading desks.

CNBC also cited Morgan Stanley in pointing to the separation of custody from execution as the more consequential structural shift, and it noted that the stress could drive consolidation as companies buy capabilities and chase scale.

For investors, the useful move is to read the next round of earnings calls and disclosures for custody-related language, because that language will show whether firms are winning the shift or just talking about it.
We searched for hard evidence of a price reaction in listed custody and infrastructure names and found none we could verify.

Additionally, Treasury yields dropped as heightened oversight dampens fiscal stimulus hopes, while cryptocurrencies also fell amid uncertainty surrounding upcoming industry regulations.

extraction.body: Regulatory jitters and state-level data center hurdles spark Asia-wide tech selloff Asian stock and foreign exchange markets swung on the 4th after Democrats won majorities in both the U.S. Senate and House in the midterm elections. As concerns spread that a Democrat-controlled Congress may tighten regulations on artificial intelligence (AI) and the cryptocurrency industry, and that key State Governments could revisit data center policies, Asian semiconductor and AI-related shares fell across the board. As U.S. Government Bonds yields fell, the dollar weakened in tandem. As the results of the U.S. midterm election held the previous day were reported during Asian trading hours on the 4th (local time), AI-related stocks slumped across Asian markets, including Korea and Japan. In the Korea Exchange (KRX) stock market, Samsung Electronics(005930) and SK hynix(000660) , which had risen in the 3% and 5% ranges in early trading, respectively, ended slightly lower. In the Tokyo Stock Exchange, semiconductor bellwether Kioxia fell 5.4%. TSMC, which accounts for 40% of Taiwan Stock Exchange weighting, slipped 1.5%. U.S. stock index futures also fell sharply in premarket trading before paring some losses. Charu Chanana, Saxo's chief investment strategist, told Reuters that "market investors are pricing in a stronger-than-expected Democratic surge," adding that "Democratic strength could lower expectations for additional fiscal stimulus." With control of Congress shifting to Democrats, the likelihood of federal-level probes and legislative regulations targeting big tech and the cryptocurrency industry has grown. Jake Dollarhide, Longbow Asset Management CEO, said, "Democratic control of Congress is a headwind for tech stocks and could exert potential regulatory pressure across all AI fields," adding, "It could slow the AI growth we take for granted." Nick Peles, Vantagepoint Asset Management CIO, also said, "The risk factor is tighter regulation across the AI and cryptocurrency ecosystems." Tim Sun, HashKey senior researcher, likewise said, "The shift in the U.S. political landscape could delay cryptocurrency legislation and the creation of an institutional framework," adding, "All of this is acting as a strong headwind for the cryptocurrency market." In particular, markets flagged potential permitting and power supply disruptions for data centers stemming from the Texas and Georgia gubernatorial election results, rather than federal-level policies, as a new key risk. Even if U.S. President Donald Trump vetoes congressional bills, approvals for data center construction and power grid connections are dictated by State Governments. Tapas Strickland, Moomoo Australia-New Zealand chief market strategist, said, "There are significant concerns that the pace of AI infrastructure buildout could slow considerably as we assess how Texas will exercise its authority over AI-related policies," adding, "Texas and Georgia together account for roughly one-third of total AI data center expenditure and projects; if both states seat Democratic governors, the likelihood of a moderation in pace is very high and could set off ripple effects across the broader AI industry." However, some analysts said the sharp drop in Asian semiconductor stocks tied to these U.S. political variables is merely a reaction to short-term risk-off sentiment, and is far removed from any real hit to sales or order performance for Asian chipmakers, including those in Korea. Rather than an immediate pullback in big tech capital spending, political uncertainty has piled onto recent debates about an AI peak over the past few weeks, triggering short-term selling, they said. Kazunori Datebe, Daiwa Asset Management chief strategist, said, "Japanese AI stocks are already cheap, and corporate earnings are solid, so the downside should be limited."

extraction.body: Regulatory jitters and state-level data center hurdles spark Asia-wide tech selloff Asian stock and foreign exchange markets swung on the 4th after Democrats won majorities in both the U.S. Senate and House in the midterm elections. As concerns spread that a Democrat-controlled Congress may tighten regulations on artificial intelligence (AI) and the cryptocurrency industry, and that key State Governments could revisit data center policies, Asian semiconductor and AI-related shares fell across the board. As U.S. Government Bonds yields fell, the dollar weakened in tandem. As the results of the U.S. midterm election held the previous day were reported during Asian trading hours on the 4th (local time), AI-related stocks slumped across Asian markets, including Korea and Japan. In the Korea Exchange (KRX) stock market, Samsung Electronics(005930) and SK hynix(000660) , which had risen in the 3% and 5% ranges in early trading, respectively, ended slightly lower. In the Tokyo Stock Exchange, semiconductor bellwether Kioxia fell 5.4%. TSMC, which accounts for 40% of Taiwan Stock Exchange weighting, slipped 1.5%. U.S. stock index futures also fell sharply in premarket trading before paring some losses. Charu Chanana, Saxo's chief investment strategist, told Reuters that "market investors are pricing in a stronger-than-expected Democratic surge," adding that "Democratic strength could lower expectations for additional fiscal stimulus." With control of Congress shifting to Democrats, the likelihood of federal-level probes and legislative regulations targeting big tech and the cryptocurrency industry has grown. Jake Dollarhide, Longbow Asset Management CEO, said, "Democratic control of Congress is a headwind for tech stocks and could exert potential regulatory pressure across all AI fields," adding, "It could slow the AI growth we take for granted." Nick Peles, Vantagepoint Asset Management CIO, also said, "The risk factor is tighter regulation across the AI and cryptocurrency ecosystems." Tim Sun, HashKey senior researcher, likewise said, "The shift in the U.S. political landscape could delay cryptocurrency legislation and the creation of an institutional framework," adding, "All of this is acting as a strong headwind for the cryptocurrency market." In particular, markets flagged potential permitting and power supply disruptions for data centers stemming from the Texas and Georgia gubernatorial election results, rather than federal-level policies, as a new key risk. Even if U.S. President Donald Trump vetoes congressional bills, approvals for data center construction and power grid connections are dictated by State Governments. Tapas Strickland, Moomoo Australia-New Zealand chief market strategist, said, "There are significant concerns that the pace of AI infrastructure buildout could slow considerably as we assess how Texas will exercise its authority over AI-related policies," adding, "Texas and Georgia together account for roughly one-third of total AI data center expenditure and projects; if both states seat Democratic governors, the likelihood of a moderation in pace is very high and could set off ripple effects across the broader AI industry." However, some analysts said the sharp drop in Asian semiconductor stocks tied to these U.S. political variables is merely a reaction to short-term risk-off sentiment, and is far removed from any real hit to sales or order performance for Asian chipmakers, including those in Korea. Rather than an immediate pullback in big tech capital spending, political uncertainty has piled onto recent debates about an AI peak over the past few weeks, triggering short-term selling, they said. Kazunori Datebe, Daiwa Asset Management chief strategist, said, "Japanese AI stocks are already cheap, and corporate earnings are solid, so the downside should be limited."

extraction.body: ILULISSAT, Greenland (AP) — Greenlandic lawmakers on Tuesday voted to approve an agreement between the Arctic island, Denmark and the United States to strengthen security in the Arctic and North Atlantic after months of pressure by U.S. President Donald Trump seeking to control the semiautonomous territory of a NATO ally. The trilateral deal paves the way for more U.S. bases in Greenland and eases tensions over Trump’s repeated calls for the vast island to become part of the United States. The agreement’s goal is to bolster the U.S. military presence on Greenland but keep the self-governing island under Danish control. It would still apply if Greenland eventually chose independence. Greenlandic lawmakers voted 16-0 for the agreement, with seven abstentions, in the capital city of Nuuk. Some 570 kilometers (350 miles) north of Nuuk, Nukaaka Lund-Mathaeussen hoped that the deal’s approval means the Trump administration “got what they wanted.” “Hopefully after this we won’t be getting underhanded threats from the American government,” the 28-year-old Ilulissat resident told The Associated Press in Ilulissat after the vote. William Tukula, a 34-year-old chef in Ilulissat, said he’d seen posts on Facebook from older Greenlanders who were “a little bit scared about Trump and soldiers.” The U.S. president had previously said he would not rule out the use of military force to seize control of Greenland because he declared U.S. control of it to be vital to American national security, though he also underlined his support for Greenlanders determining their own future. He later backed down from any threat. The White House had no immediate comment on the vote, but the State Department said it “marks another major victory for American national security.” “This administration is securing America’s strategic interests in the Arctic, strengthening our national defense and ensuring this critical region remains free of adversarial threats,” it said in a post on X. Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed the security agreement in September on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York. Nielsen, in a post on Facebook after Tuesday’s vote, said Greenlanders stood united over the last few months despite the geopolitical tensions to show the world that the island decides its own fate. “We must be able to cooperate with other countries,” he wrote, adding that the cooperation must respect “our people, our country and our rights.” He added: “Greenland is our country. Greenland will always be our country.” Danish lawmakers are set to debate it later this month. The deal will “enter into force” once the “necessary parliamentary processes of the Kingdom of Denmark, in conjunction with Greenland, have been completed.” Despite the Greenland parliament’s approval, Lund-Mathaeussen said some residents on the island felt worried and powerless. “What can a regular guy like me do about the diplomatic engine?” the municipality worker said. “It’s a big machine, and being a small person here in Greenland — it’s hard to have any influences on those things.” Nukaaraq Thomsen, a 43-year-old incineration plant worker from Ilulissat, said the trilateral deal still won’t benefit Greenlanders. “My opinion is it’s safe for Greenland. But not for the people — only for the land,” Thomsen told the AP on Tuesday. In expanding its military presence on the island, the agreement says Washington is to award contracts for goods and services related to setting up, maintaining or dismantling such bases “to Greenlandic sources to the maximum extent possible.” But Lars Erik Gabrielsen, mayor of Avannaata Municipality, is not convinced that Greenlanders will see any advantages. “It’s a good deal for Denmark, NATO. Not a good deal for us,” he said. “There are no benefits, no money to our society. The agreement was signed in September by U.S. President Donald Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Greenlandic lawmakers voted 16-0 for the agreement, with seven abstentions, and the deal was described as strengthening security in the Arctic and North Atlantic while keeping Greenland under Danish control.
Mute Egede framed the ratification as a step forward for the self-governing island, writing, “The road to this point has been a difficult one for us as a people.”
The agreement’s entry into force was tied to Denmark and Greenland completing “necessary parliamentary processes of the Kingdom of Denmark, in conjunction with Greenland.”
Opposition party members questioned the deal’s economic value even as the agreement advanced, with Reuters describing that some lawmakers raised concerns about what the arrangement would be worth.

Pele Broberg, chair of the pro-independence Naleraq party, said, “We are looking for a better agreement that we can benefit from when we become an independent state. But no economic benefit has been gained from the agreement.”
DW reported that Greenland’s Foreign Minister Mute Egede told lawmakers, “We must accept that peace and stability are no longer something we can take for granted,” shortly before the vote in Nuuk.

The agreement was presented as alleviating pressure after Trump’s repeated threats to take control of the self-governing Danish territory, and it was also described as easing tensions over calls for Greenland to become part of the United States.

He later backed down from any threat. General Assembly in New York. The trilateral deal paves the way for more U.S. bases in Greenland and eases tensions over Trump’s repeated calls for the vast island to become part of the United States.
The agreement’s goal is to bolster the U.S. military presence on Greenland but keep the self-governing island under Danish control. It would still apply if Greenland eventually chose independence.
Greenlandic lawmakers voted 16-0 for the agreement, with seven abstentions, in the capital city of Nuuk.
Some 570 kilometers (350 miles) north of Nuuk, Nukaaka Lund-Mathaeussen hoped that the deal’s approval means the Trump administration “got what they wanted.”
“Hopefully after this we won’t be getting underhanded threats from the American government,” the 28-year-old Ilulissat resident told The Associated Press in Ilulissat after the vote.
William Tukula, a 34-year-old chef in Ilulissat, said he’d seen posts on Facebook from older Greenlanders who were “a little bit scared about Trump and soldiers.”

The U.S. president had previously said he would not rule out the use of military force to seize control of Greenland because he declared U.S. control of it to be vital to American national security, though he also underlined his support for Greenlanders determining their own future. He later backed down from any threat.
The White House had no immediate comment on the vote, but the State Department said it “marks another major victory for American national security.”

“This administration is securing America’s strategic interests in the Arctic, strengthening our national defense and ensuring this critical region remains free of adversarial threats,” it said in a post on X.

Trump, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen signed the security agreement in September on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly in New York.
Nielsen, in a post on Facebook after Tuesday’s vote, said Greenlanders stood united over the last few months despite the geopolitical tensions to show the world that the island decides its own fate.
“We must be able to cooperate with other countries,” he wrote, adding that the cooperation must respect “our people, our country and our rights.”
He added: “Greenland is our country. Greenland will always be our country.”

Danish lawmakers are set to debate it later this month. The deal will “enter into force” once the “necessary parliamentary processes of the Kingdom of Denmark, in conjunction with Greenland, have been completed.”

Despite the Greenland parliament’s approval, Lund-Mathaeussen said some residents on the island felt worried and powerless. “What can a regular guy like me do about the diplomatic engine?” the municipality worker said. “It’s a big machine, and being a small person here in Greenland — it’s hard to have any influences on those things.”
Nukaaraq Thomsen, a 43-year-old incineration plant worker from Ilulissat, said the trilateral deal still won’t benefit Greenlanders.
“My opinion is it’s safe for Greenland. But not for the people — only for the land,” Thomsen told the AP on Tuesday.

In expanding its military presence on the island, the agreement says Washington is to award contracts for goods and services related to setting up, maintaining or dismantling such bases “to Greenlandic sources to the maximum extent possible.”
But Lars Erik Gabrielsen, mayor of Avannaata Municipality, is not convinced that Greenlanders will see any advantages.
“It’s a good deal for Denmark, NATO. Not a good deal for us,” he said. “There are no benefits, no money to our society. Zero.”

The deal will “enter into force” once the “necessary parliamentary processes of the Kingdom of Denmark, in conjunction with Greenland, have been completed.” The agreement's goal is to bolster the U.S. military presence on Greenland but keep the self-governing island under Danish control. It would still apply if Greenland eventually chooses independence.

Google has released security fixes for a critical Android vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute code on a device without requiring any interaction from the user.
Devices with the Android security patch level dated November 1, 2026, or later include the fix.
The flaw affects Android code responsible for decoding WAP Push messages delivered through SMS.

Google had not reported any known exploitation of the vulnerability as of November 4, and the flaw was not listed in the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue as of its November 3 update.
Google’s November Android security bulletin addresses 216 vulnerabilities in total.
Devices running Android 10 or later can receive some security fixes through Google Play system updates.
The public bulletin and CVE record do not explain how an attacker would reach the vulnerable code path.
Google’s severity assessment assumes that Android’s built-in security protections and Google services are either disabled or successfully bypassed.
Google uses separate patch dates so device manufacturers can distribute fixes for common Android components more quickly.
The company encourages manufacturers to include all available fixes wherever possible.
Several Critical vulnerabilities were also fixed in the Android kernel.
The malformed message reportedly does not appear in the normal message inbox.

The November update nevertheless highlights the importance of keeping Android devices current, particularly when flaws can potentially be exploited remotely without requiring a victim to open a file, install an application or interact with a malicious message.
Twenty-three of those issues are rated Critical.

extraction.body: Google has released security fixes for a critical Android vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute code on a device without requiring any interaction from the user. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-58868, affects Android versions 14 through 17 and was addressed in Google’s November 2026 Android security update. Devices with the Android security patch level dated November 1, 2026, or later include the fix. Google had not reported any known exploitation of the vulnerability as of November 4, and the flaw was not listed in the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue as of its November 3 update. CVE-2026-58868 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability caused by a heap buffer overflow in the onOutputReceived function of Android’s FrameDecoder.cpp . Google classified the issue as Critical because, under certain conditions, it could allow remote code execution without additional execution privileges or user interaction. The public bulletin and CVE record do not explain how an attacker would reach the vulnerable code path. Google’s severity assessment assumes that Android’s built-in security protections and Google services are either disabled or successfully bypassed. Older Android versions, including Android 12 and Android 13, are not listed as affected by CVE-2026-58868. However, the available records do not clarify whether the same vulnerable code exists in those releases. Google’s November bulletin uses two security patch levels. Devices with the 2026-11-05 patch level include all fixes from the November bulletin, including vulnerabilities affecting the Android kernel and components supplied by Arm, Imagination Technologies, MediaTek, Unisoc and Qualcomm. Google uses separate patch dates so device manufacturers can distribute fixes for common Android components more quickly. The company encourages manufacturers to include all available fixes wherever possible. Users can check their patch level by opening the device Settings menu, selecting About phone or About tablet, and viewing the Android security update date. The November bulletin also includes CVE-2026-58882, another Critical vulnerability that could allow a remote denial-of-service attack without user interaction. The flaw affects Android code responsible for decoding WAP Push messages delivered through SMS. A researcher who publishes under the name Mark B recently described a flaw in the same function as an “SMS of Death.” According to that research, a specially crafted WAP Push message could crash the com.android.phone process, terminating active calls, including potentially emergency calls. The malformed message reportedly does not appear in the normal message inbox. Researchers also reported that a vulnerable phone could repeatedly process the malicious message after restarting, potentially causing repeated crashes until the message is removed. Google’s security bulletin does not explicitly state whether CVE-2026-58882 is the same vulnerability described in that public research. Google’s November Android security bulletin addresses 216 vulnerabilities in total. Twenty-three of those issues are rated Critical. In addition to CVE-2026-58868, two other Critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936, affect Android’s System component and could potentially allow remote code execution. Several Critical vulnerabilities were also fixed in the Android kernel. Two of those affect Bluetooth-related code, while the most severe kernel issue could allow a remote attacker to obtain elevated privileges without user interaction. The November 5 patch level also includes fixes for Critical vulnerabilities in MediaTek modem components and a closed-source Qualcomm component. MediaTek said it was not aware of active exploitation of the Critical modem vulnerabilities covered in its November security bulletin. Devices running Android 10 or later can receive some security fixes through Google Play system updates. The November Google Play update list includes CVE-2026-58876, another Critical vulnerability. However, CVE-2026-58868 is not included in that mechanism. Users specifically concerned about CVE-2026-58868 should therefore check the Android security patch date on their device rather than relying only on the Google Play system update date. A security patch level of November 1, 2026, or later covers the flaw. That distinction is important because the vulnerability represents a potentially serious attack path, but there is currently no evidence that it is being actively weaponised. The November update nevertheless highlights the importance of keeping Android devices current, particularly when flaws can potentially be exploited remotely without requiring a victim to open a file, install an application or interact with a malicious message. About the author — Suvedita Nath is a science student with a growing interest in cybercrime and digital safety. She writes on online activity, cyber threats, and technology-driven risks. Her work focuses on clarity, accuracy, and public awareness. The420.in delivers the latest news, investigative reports and expert insights on cybercrime, corruption, economic fraud, technology and public policy. We keep you informed about the issues that matter.

Fixes reach devices through each manufacturer's own update schedule, so most Android devices will not have them yet.

extraction.body: Status: Google published the Android Security Bulletin for November 2026 on 2 November 2026. Security patch level 2026-11-05 or later addresses every issue in it. Google has not reported exploitation of any of these vulnerabilities. As of our 4 November 2026 check, none of the 216 CVEs listed is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. Fixes reach devices through each manufacturer's own update schedule, so most Android devices will not have them yet. The November 2026 Android Security Bulletin ( Android Security Bulletin—November 2026 ) lists 216 CVEs: 23 rated Critical and 193 rated High. In Google's words, the most severe is "a critical security vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation." That issue is CVE-2026-58868 . Two more Critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws sit in the System component: CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936 . The second patch level adds eight Critical issues in MediaTek modem components, six Critical Linux kernel issues and one Critical issue in a Qualcomm closed-source component. Some context keeps this in proportion. Google's ratings describe what exploitation "would possibly" do "assuming the platform and service mitigations are turned off for development purposes or if successfully bypassed." The bulletin says nothing about attacks in the wild, and CISA's SSVC entries on the NVD records for the three Critical RCEs say "Exploitation: none." We rate this advisory High . A remote code execution flaw that needs no user interaction is serious enough to plan for now. We do not rate it Critical, because nobody has reported exploitation and the platform mitigations still stand between a bug and a working attack. For third-party risk teams, the problem is not one patch. It is how long patches take to arrive. Google's bulletin is only the start. Each phone and tablet maker then builds, tests and ships its own update, and many older or low-cost devices never get one. Vendors whose staff read your email, approve payments, run MDM or field-service apps, or hold your data on Android devices inherit that lag. Bulletin published (confirmed). Google published the bulletin (version 1.0) on 2 November 2026. It says: "Security patch levels of 2026-11-05 or later address all of these issues." Google adds that it notifies "Android partners of all issues at least a month before publishing the bulletin." It also says that "within 48 hours after the initial publication of this bulletin," Google will publish the source code patches to the Android Open Source Project (AOSP) and then update the bulletin with the AOSP links. When we fetched the bulletin on 4 November 2026 at 09:13 Asia/Nicosia (UTC+2), it was still version 1.0. CVE records (confirmed). NVD published the CVE records on 2 November 2026 at about 22:17 Asia/Nicosia (20:17 UTC). On 4 November, CVE-2026-58868, CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936 were all "Awaiting Analysis," with no CVSS score from either NVD or the CNA. Google's bulletin uses its own Critical/High/Moderate ratings rather than CVSS, so this advisory cites no CVSS numbers ( NVD CVE-2026-58868 ). Exploitation status. No exploitation has been reported. This bulletin has no note about "limited, targeted exploitation," the wording Google uses when it knows of active attacks. None of the 216 CVEs appears in CISA KEV (catalog version 2026.11.03, checked 4 November 2026). CISA's SSVC entries for the three Critical RCEs record Exploitation "none," Automatable "yes" and Technical impact "total." "Automatable" is the reason to prepare now rather than at the next routine patch cycle. It is not evidence of attacks. We will update this post if Google, CISA or a chipset vendor reports exploitation. The bulletin sorts fixes into two security patch levels, and that split matters when you check vendor answers: A device reporting 2026-11-01 has the Framework and System fixes but may still lack the kernel and chipset fixes. Only 2026-11-05 or later covers everything in this bulletin. Each CVE record says the flaw "could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation." The descriptions point at media and image handling (a frame decoder and PNG processing), where an attacker controls the incoming content. The bulletin does not say which delivery paths, such as messaging, browsing or file previews, reach the vulnerable code. We will not guess. No proof-of-concept has been published, and we do not describe how these flaws could be exploited. The bulletin's Google Play system updates list puts CVE-2026-58876 under the Media Codecs Mainline component. Devices that get Google Play system updates may therefore receive that fix through Google Play, separately from the manufacturer's full firmware update. Google notes that "for some devices on Android 10 or later, the Google Play system update will have a date string that matches the 2026-11-01 security patch level." The bulletin does not place CVE-2026-58868 or CVE-2026-58936 on that list, so those two depend on the manufacturer's update. The System component also has five more Critical issues: three elevation-of-privilege flaws (CVE-2026-55275, CVE-2026-55283, CVE-2026-58984) and two denial-of-service flaws (CVE-2026-58814, CVE-2026-58882). The Framework section lists one more RCE, CVE-2026-58857, which Google rates High. The remaining entries are rated High. They cover Arm Mali and CPU, Imagination PowerVR GPU, Unisoc modem and uboot, and Qualcomm components. Our full table of every CVE listed on the bulletin is kept with this advisory's working notes. The authoritative list is the bulletin itself. AOSP bulletin vs. OEM rollout. The bulletin is not a firmware release for your devices. The November 2026 Android Security Bulletin ( Android Security Bulletin—November 2026 ) lists 216 CVEs: 23 rated Critical and 193 rated High. In Google's words, the most severe is "a critical security vulnerability in the Framework component that could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation." That issue is CVE-2026-58868 .

Two more Critical remote code execution (RCE) flaws sit in the System component: CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936 . The second patch level adds eight Critical issues in MediaTek modem components, six Critical Linux kernel issues and one Critical issue in a Qualcomm closed-source component.

Google's ratings describe what exploitation "would possibly" do "assuming the platform and service mitigations are turned off for development purposes or if successfully bypassed." A remote code execution flaw that needs no user interaction is serious enough to plan for now. We do not rate it Critical, because nobody has reported exploitation and the platform mitigations still stand between a bug and a working attack.

extraction.body: A critical Android flaw could allow an attacker to run code on a phone without any user action remotely, Google said in its November security bulletin . The flaw, CVE-2026-58868 , affects Android 14 through 17. Phones get the fix with security patch level 2026-11-01 or later, which phone makers and carriers send on their own schedules. As of November 4, Google's bulletin did not report any attacks exploiting its flaws. None of them was in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, kept by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, as of its November 3 update. The flaw is a possible out-of-bounds write caused by a heap buffer overflow in the onOutputReceived function of the file FrameDecoder.cpp. Neither the bulletin nor the flaw's CVE record says how an attacker would reach that code. Google's Critical rating assumes that the protections built into Android and Google's services are turned off or bypassed. Older versions, such as Android 12 and 13, are not listed as affected by the flaw. Google's records do not say whether they contain it. The Android security update date is the phone's security patch level. A date of 2026-11-01 or later covers CVE-2026-58868 and the other flaws in the Framework, System, and Android runtime components. A date of 2026-11-05 or later covers every flaw in the November bulletin, including those in the kernel and in parts from Arm, Imagination Technologies, MediaTek, Unisoc and Qualcomm. Google sets two dates so phone makers can ship a set of fixes common to all Android devices sooner. It encourages them to include every fix in the bulletin. Phones running Android 10 or later may also receive some fixes through Google Play system updates. This month's list for those updates includes another Critical flaw, CVE-2026-58876. CVE-2026-58868 is not on that list, so the date to check for it is the Android security update. The bulletin gives no workaround for phones that cannot install the update yet. Another Critical flaw, CVE-2026-58882, could allow a remote denial-of-service attack with no user interaction, according to its CVE record . It is in decodeWapPdu, a function in Android's code for WAP Push messages that arrive via SMS. On October 29, a researcher who publishes as Mark B posted a write-up called "SMS of Death" about a bug in the same function. Neither the bulletin nor the CVE record says whether CVE-2026-58882 is that bug. One malformed WAP Push message crashes com.android.phone and ends any active call, including emergency calls, according to the write-up. In tests on several phone models, the crash happened every time. The attacker needs only the target's phone number, and the message never shows up in the inbox. The phone retries the message each time it starts, so it can crash on startup until the message is removed. A proof-of-concept app that sends such a message from one phone to another is public. Phones running Android 12 and 13 run the same code but do not receive the fix that newer versions do, the researcher says. Google's November bulletin lists 216 vulnerabilities, 23 of them rated Critical. Two more Critical flaws could allow remote code execution: CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936, both in Android's System component. Six Critical flaws are in the kernel, two of them in Bluetooth code. The most severe kernel flaw could allow a remote attacker to gain elevated privileges without user interaction. The 2026-11-05 patch level also fixes Critical flaws in MediaTek modem code and in a closed-source Qualcomm component. In its November bulletin , MediaTek describes its Critical modem flaws as out-of-bounds writes and says it is not aware of any active exploitation. extraction.body: Google has released security fixes for a critical Android vulnerability that could allow a remote attacker to execute code on a device without requiring any interaction from the user. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-58868, affects Android versions 14 through 17 and was addressed in Google’s November 2026 Android security update. Devices with the Android security patch level dated November 1, 2026, or later include the fix. Google had not reported any known exploitation of the vulnerability as of November 4, and the flaw was not listed in the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency’s Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue as of its November 3 update. CVE-2026-58868 is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability caused by a heap buffer overflow in the onOutputReceived function of Android’s FrameDecoder.cpp . Google classified the issue as Critical because, under certain conditions, it could allow remote code execution without additional execution privileges or user interaction. The public bulletin and CVE record do not explain how an attacker would reach the vulnerable code path. Google’s severity assessment assumes that Android’s built-in security protections and Google services are either disabled or successfully bypassed. Older Android versions, including Android 12 and Android 13, are not listed as affected by CVE-2026-58868. However, the available records do not clarify whether the same vulnerable code exists in those releases. Google’s November bulletin uses two security patch levels. Devices with the 2026-11-05 patch level include all fixes from the November bulletin, including vulnerabilities affecting the Android kernel and components supplied by Arm, Imagination Technologies, MediaTek, Unisoc and Qualcomm. Google uses separate patch dates so device manufacturers can distribute fixes for common Android components more quickly. The company encourages manufacturers to include all available fixes wherever possible. Users can check their patch level by opening the device Settings menu, selecting About phone or About tablet, and viewing the Android security update date. The November bulletin also includes CVE-2026-58882, another Critical vulnerability that could allow a remote denial-of-service attack without user interaction. The flaw affects Android code responsible for decoding WAP Push messages delivered through SMS. A researcher who publishes under the name Mark B recently described a flaw in the same function as an “SMS of Death.” According to that research, a specially crafted WAP Push message could crash the com.android.phone process, terminating active calls, including potentially emergency calls. The malformed message reportedly does not appear in the normal message inbox. Researchers also reported that a vulnerable phone could repeatedly process the malicious message after restarting, potentially causing repeated crashes until the message is removed. Google’s security bulletin does not explicitly state whether CVE-2026-58882 is the same vulnerability described in that public research. Google’s November Android security bulletin addresses 216 vulnerabilities in total. Twenty-three of those issues are rated Critical. In addition to CVE-2026-58868, two other Critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936, affect Android’s System component and could potentially allow remote code execution. Several Critical vulnerabilities were also fixed in the Android kernel. Two of those affect Bluetooth-related code, while the most severe kernel issue could allow a remote attacker to obtain elevated privileges without user interaction. The November 5 patch level also includes fixes for Critical vulnerabilities in MediaTek modem components and a closed-source Qualcomm component. MediaTek said it was not aware of active exploitation of the Critical modem vulnerabilities covered in its November security bulletin. Devices running Android 10 or later can receive some security fixes through Google Play system updates. The November Google Play update list includes CVE-2026-58876, another Critical vulnerability. However, CVE-2026-58868 is not included in that mechanism. Users specifically concerned about CVE-2026-58868 should therefore check the Android security patch date on their device rather than relying only on the Google Play system update date. A security patch level of November 1, 2026, or later covers the flaw. That distinction is important because the vulnerability represents a potentially serious attack path, but there is currently no evidence that it is being actively weaponised. The November update nevertheless highlights the importance of keeping Android devices current, particularly when flaws can potentially be exploited remotely without requiring a victim to open a file, install an application or interact with a malicious message. extraction.body: A critical Android flaw could allow an attacker to run code on a phone without any user action remotely, Google said in its November security bulletin . The flaw, CVE-2026-58868 , affects Android 14 through 17. Phones get the fix with security patch level 2026-11-01 or later, which phone makers and carriers send on their own schedules. As of November 4, Google's bulletin did not report any attacks exploiting its flaws. None of them was in the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, kept by the U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, as of its November 3 update. The flaw is a possible out-of-bounds write caused by a heap buffer overflow in the onOutputReceived function of the file FrameDecoder.cpp. Neither the bulletin nor the flaw's CVE record says how an attacker would reach that code. Google's Critical rating assumes that the protections built into Android and Google's services are turned off or bypassed. Older versions, such as Android 12 and 13, are not listed as affected by the flaw. Google's records do not say whether they contain it. The Android security update date is the phone's security patch level. A date of 2026-11-01 or later covers CVE-2026-58868 and the other flaws in the Framework, System, and Android runtime components. A date of 2026-11-05 or later covers every flaw in the November bulletin, including those in the kernel and in parts from Arm, Imagination Technologies, MediaTek, Unisoc and Qualcomm. Google sets two dates so phone makers can ship a set of fixes common to all Android devices sooner. It encourages them to include every fix in the bulletin. Phones running Android 10 or later may also receive some fixes through Google Play system updates. This month's list for those updates includes another Critical flaw, CVE-2026-58876. CVE-2026-58868 is not on that list, so the date to check for it is the Android security update. The bulletin gives no workaround for phones that cannot install the update yet. Another Critical flaw, CVE-2026-58882, could allow a remote denial-of-service attack with no user interaction, according to its CVE record . It is in decodeWapPdu, a function in Android's code for WAP Push messages that arrive via SMS. On October 29, a researcher who publishes as Mark B posted a write-up called "SMS of Death" about a bug in the same function. Neither the bulletin nor the CVE record says whether CVE-2026-58882 is that bug. One malformed WAP Push message crashes com.android.phone and ends any active call, including emergency calls, according to the write-up. In tests on several phone models, the crash happened every time. The attacker needs only the target's phone number, and the message never shows up in the inbox. The phone retries the message each time it starts, so it can crash on startup until the message is removed. A proof-of-concept app that sends such a message from one phone to another is public. Phones running Android 12 and 13 run the same code but do not receive the fix that newer versions do, the researcher says. Google's November bulletin lists 216 vulnerabilities, 23 of them rated Critical. Two more Critical flaws could allow remote code execution: CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936, both in Android's System component. Six Critical flaws are in the kernel, two of them in Bluetooth code. The most severe kernel flaw could allow a remote attacker to gain elevated privileges without user interaction. The 2026-11-05 patch level also fixes Critical flaws in MediaTek modem code and in a closed-source Qualcomm component. In its November bulletin , MediaTek describes its Critical modem flaws as out-of-bounds writes and says it is not aware of any active exploitation. A proof-of-concept app that sends such a message from one phone to another is public. Phones running Android 12 and 13 run the same code but do not receive the fix that newer versions do, the researcher says.

Google's November bulletin lists 216 vulnerabilities, 23 of them rated Critical. Two more Critical flaws could allow remote code execution: CVE-2026-58876 and CVE-2026-58936, both in Android's System component.
Six Critical flaws are in the kernel, two of them in Bluetooth code. The most severe kernel flaw could allow a remote attacker to gain elevated privileges without user interaction.

The 2026-11-05 patch level also fixes Critical flaws in MediaTek modem code and in a closed-source Qualcomm component. In its November bulletin , MediaTek describes its Critical modem flaws as out-of-bounds writes and says it is not aware of any active exploitation.

passages: 03, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Crytica Security , developer of the world's first Rapid Detection, Alert and isolation (RDAi™) solution, and Carahsoft Technology Corp. , The Trusted Government IT Solutions Provider®, today announced a distribution partnership that moves OT threat detection from the network into the device itself.
Under the agreement, Carahsoft will serve as a Public Sector distributor for Crytica, making RDAi available to Federal agencies and State, Local and Education (SLED) organizations across the U.S.
Public Sector through Carahsoft's reseller partners and NASA Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP V) and National Association of State Procurement Officials (NASPO) ValuePoint contracts.

"Partnering with Carahsoft provides Crytica Security with the broad Government reach that allows us to accelerate the deployment of our patented RDAi technology within Federal, State and Local Governments and Educational institutions,” said C.
Lloyd Mahaffey, Executive Chairman and Co-Founder of Crytica Security.
"We are pleased to work together to help protect millions of critical infrastructure devices in the United States.”

From military installations and Federal facilities to municipal water systems, public power utilities, transit networks and university campuses, Public Sector OT is a sustained target for nation-state actors seeking persistent access to critical infrastructure.
Many OT security solutions rely on network monitoring, asset discovery and behavioral analysis to detect potential threats.
These capabilities provide important visibility but are not designed to deterministically detect unauthorized changes to the instruction sets running inside the devices themselves.
RDAi adds a complementary layer of detection by monitoring device instruction sets directly.
Its Probe, as small as 70KB, detects unauthorized changes within seconds using deterministic detection, without relying on threat signatures or behavioral analysis.

Working with resellers, systems integrators and consultants, our sales and marketing teams provide industry leading IT products, services and training through hundreds of contract vehicles.
Its alerts flow into the security platforms and workflows agencies already rely on, adding device-level evidence that helps teams respond faster and make better-informed isolation decisions.

coreStoryFacts.text: Government agencies are increasingly seeking cybersecurity solutions that deliver actionable insights, measurable outcomes and a more comprehensive understanding of risk.

Tidal Cyber's Threat-Led Defense platform provides a unique approach to aligning security operations with real-world adversary procedures, enabling organizations to prioritize resources, optimize defenses and strengthen cyber resilience.
We are pleased to partner with Carahsoft, which has supported Public Sector markets for decades, and now commercial markets as well.

Through our partnership with Carahsoft, Public and Commercial Sector organizations can now align security investments, prioritize risk and improve defensive effectiveness based on real-world attack execution.
This enables organizations to understand how attacks unfold, identify defensive gaps and prioritize actions based on actual risk.
This approach provides organizations with a level of granularity and context that has long been unavailable, enabling security teams to:

New Threat-Led Asset Visibility and Vulnerability Prioritization capabilities help security teams understand how adversaries leverage specific assets and vulnerabilities and assess their potential impact on attack campaigns.
Together, these solutions enable organizations to operationalize procedure-led intelligence across defensive security to effectively disrupt attacks across the entire kill chain.

sources.title: Google hasn’t figured out how to make AI pay like its search engine
passages: The thing is, Google, as well as competitors like OpenAI, are still figuring out how to make ads work in AI — both delivering results for advertisers and avoiding alienating the people using their AI tools.

YOY growth for search revenue vs. paid clicks in Q1-3 in 2026 “This is the first major disruption that Google is facing to its core business in decades,” Nate Elliott, an eMarketer principal analyst covering AI and advertising, tells The Verge.
However, Google’s Search revenue growth slowed to 12 percent year over year in the third quarter, down from roughly 17 percent in the previous quarter.
Search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, Google parent Alphabet said in its earnings report last week.
Meanwhile, growth in paid clicks — clicks on ads that generate revenue for Google — slowed from 13 percent to 8 percent.

He added that Google feels good about its trajectory and that its “ad experiments have shown promising results.” It remains unclear whether that reflects a deliberate rollout of ads, as Google says, or a more fundamental problem with advertising in AI search.
An October working paper found that US visits from ChatGPT ads generated 64 percent less revenue for retailers per session than visits from Google Search ads: $0.89 versus $2.45.
What Google’s core Search business looks like increasingly depends on what you ask.
Google’s claim that most AI Mode queries are additional doesn’t tell us how much revenue it could lose from the searches AI Mode replaces.
The working paper measures retailers’ sales rather than platform revenue, and its findings about ChatGPT don’t establish how Google’s own AI ads perform.
AI is changing how people find information — and whether they click on the ads that fund Google’s business.
Google is currently expanding ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode, including internationally and across multiple turns of US AI Mode conversations.
For now, advertisers are still getting results from Google.
Google doesn’t let them separately target that inventory or break out its performance, Taylor says.
The risk is that AI Mode also draws people away from searches that Google monetizes more effectively.

extraction.body: Search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, Google parent Alphabet said in its earnings report last week. However, Google’s Search revenue growth slowed to 12 percent year over year in the third quarter, down from roughly 17 percent in the previous quarter. Meanwhile, growth in paid clicks — clicks on ads that generate revenue for Google — slowed from 13 percent to 8 percent. That’s still substantial growth, but not the direction investors were hoping for from a company planning to spend about $200 billion this year on infrastructure, largely to support AI. Alphabet shares have fallen about 14 percent since it reported earnings last week, as investors question the costs and returns of the company’s AI ambitions. Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler said currency effects were the biggest driver of the revenue-growth slowdown, alongside changes in spending by advertisers in particular industries. But Google’s AI makeover also contributed to the slowdown: AI Mode queries were growing strongly but monetizing at a lower rate than traditional searches, Schindler says. He added that Google feels good about its trajectory and that its “ad experiments have shown promising results.” It remains unclear whether that reflects a deliberate rollout of ads, as Google says, or a more fundamental problem with advertising in AI search. YOY growth for search revenue vs. paid clicks in Q1-3 in 2026 “This is the first major disruption that Google is facing to its core business in decades,” Nate Elliott, an eMarketer principal analyst covering AI and advertising, tells The Verge. AI is changing how people find information — and whether they click on the ads that fund Google’s business. What Google’s core Search business looks like increasingly depends on what you ask. In many cases, AI Overviews add generated summaries to search results; electing AI Mode turns searching into a conversation. But someone searching for Nikes can still get familiar shopping listings and text ads, says Andy Taylor, vice president of research at digital advertising agency Tinuiti. Google’s argument is that AI is expanding the business. Schindler says most AI Mode queries are “incremental” — additional questions rather than replacements for existing searches. Many are also “upper-funnel,” meaning people are researching potential purchases before they know what they want. The company sees those searches as opportunities to sell more ads over time. Google is currently expanding ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode, including internationally and across multiple turns of US AI Mode conversations. It has also floated bringing ads to its standalone Gemini app, saying formats developed for AI Mode could carry over, but hasn’t announced when. The thing is, Google, as well as competitors like OpenAI, are still figuring out how to make ads work in AI — both delivering results for advertisers and avoiding alienating the people using their AI tools. For now, advertisers are still getting results from Google. Tinuiti’s same-store advertisers increased their Google paid search spending 14 percent year over year in the third quarter while maintaining their return-on-ad-spend targets. “We’re still seeing a good return, and we’re not seeing performance take a hit,” Taylor says. The catch is that advertisers can’t isolate how Google’s AI ads are doing. Google doesn’t let them separately target that inventory or break out its performance, Taylor says. Steady overall returns could mean AI ad traffic is still too small to noticeably affect the results, or that it performs similarly to existing inventory. That leaves an important question unanswered: How much will AI add to Google’s advertising business, and how much could it replace? Additional queries could bring in new revenue even if each earns less than a traditional search. The risk is that AI Mode also draws people away from searches that Google monetizes more effectively. Google’s claim that most AI Mode queries are additional doesn’t tell us how much revenue it could lose from the searches AI Mode replaces. “If people are clicking through less often,” Elliott says, “that is a challenge that they need to figure out.” The promise of conversational advertising is that people share much more about their needs than they would in a few keywords. “It’s not a slam dunk that it’s going to turn into more effective advertising,” Elliott says. An early study of ChatGPT ads suggests richer conversations don’t automatically translate into more retail sales. An October working paper found that US visits from ChatGPT ads generated 64 percent less revenue for retailers per session than visits from Google Search ads: $0.89 versus $2.45. The working paper measures retailers’ sales rather than platform revenue, and its findings about ChatGPT don’t establish how Google’s own AI ads perform. Taylor cautions that those comparisons depend on what people are searching for.

sources.title: Google’s Q2: Precise Revenue Figures, Click Claims You Can’t Check - Search Engine Journal
passages: Southern is the Senior News Writer at Search Engine Journal, where he’s covered Google, SEO, ...
Alphabet's Q2 report puts precise numbers on the overall Search business while Google's claims about clicks to the web stay round and aggregate.
Liz Reid, Google’s head of Search, stated that AI Overviews mainly remove “bounce clicks,” visits where users quickly find a fact and leave.
In an August 2025 blog post , Reid mentioned that the total organic click volume has been “relatively stable” year-over-year, with an increase in average click quality.
She also explained that Google is directing slightly more “quality clicks” to websites than a year earlier.
The post also challenged third-party reports of sharp traffic drops, attributing them to flawed methods and isolated cases.
These statements are directional comparisons without a published baseline or measurement.
In April, Pichai mentioned that “queries are at an all-time high” and repeated the query-growth link in this week’s release.
In July, Nick Fox, senior vice president of Knowledge and Information, noted that Search reached its highest usage on record during a World Cup match.
These claims highlight superlatives without providing specific counts.
Having more queries does not mean more clicks leaving Google.
Overall, all three categories lack precise counts, consistent definitions over time, splits between traditional results, AI Overviews, and AI Mode, and site-level click reporting for AI features.
Search Console’s generative AI reports , accessible to some websites, show impressions without clicks , including details by page, country, and device type, but no click-through rates.
However, Google didn’t specify the exact contribution of each vertical.
Fox shared in a July LinkedIn post that AI features in Search send billions of clicks to websites weekly.
Still, Alphabet’s upcoming quarterly report will offer a snapshot of revenue, regardless of these missing details.
The earnings reports from the past three quarters haven’t included AI-feature traffic data, and Google hasn’t suggested it will include this information in the future.
The numbers also leave out part of the story.
They show us something a bit narrower: Search revenue can go up without revealing whether organic visits increased or decreased.
The revenue aspect of Search offers everything you’d hope for from a data source.

Get the channel-by-channel retail benchmarks before Black Friday. Webinar: State Of Agentic AEO For 2027: What’s Scaling & What’s Stalling Alphabet's Q2 report puts precise numbers on the overall Search business while Google's claims about clicks to the web stay round and aggregate. Here's what that gap looks like. Alphabet shared its Q2 earnings this week, showing that Google Search & Other revenue increased by 17% year over year to reach $63.27 billion. For all the details, check out our earnings brief , including how the growth rate has slowed from 19% in Q1, marking the first slowdown after four quarters of accelerating growth. The numbers also leave out part of the story. Alphabet provides a detailed breakdown of Search business earnings in its securities filing, while Google describes what the web gets back in broad assurances. Both perspectives are now part of every quarter, and the distance between them is the story. The revenue aspect of Search offers everything you’d hope for from a data source. Alphabet provided clear numbers, comparisons year-over-year, and consistent definitions across quarters, making it straightforward to follow the progress. The trajectory is checkable: Search & Other growth went from 10% in Q1 2025 to 12%, then 15%, 17%, and reaching 19% in Q1 2026 , before easing back to 17% this quarter. In its earnings release, CEO Sundar Pichai connected these results to AI, saying the company’s “popular AI features are driving Search query growth.” Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler pointed out strengths across different industries, with retail leading the way, followed by finance, technology, media, and entertainment, and credited the Gemini integration within Google’s advertising systems. However, Google didn’t specify the exact contribution of each vertical. The spending side got the same precise treatment. Roger Montti covered this , including the capital expenditures that led to negative free cash flow for the quarter. That said, none of this detailed financial data addresses the most important question for businesses: the number of clicks to websites. Neither the Q4 2025 nor Q1 2026 reports we covered offered this information. Google’s broader claims about outbound traffic come from other sources like blog posts, interviews, and social media updates from its executives. Google’s public statements about website traffic can be grouped into three categories. By organizing them this way, we see what kind of data each one would need to be testable. The first group includes usage claims. In April, Pichai mentioned that “queries are at an all-time high” and repeated the query-growth link in this week’s release. In July, Nick Fox, senior vice president of Knowledge and Information, noted that Search reached its highest usage on record during a World Cup match. These claims highlight superlatives without providing specific counts. Having more queries does not mean more clicks leaving Google. The second group involves volume claims. Fox shared in a July LinkedIn post that AI features in Search send billions of clicks to websites weekly. He also mentioned the previous daily figure: “Actually, as we’ve shared before, we continue to send billions of clicks to the web every day through Search.” However, both numbers only specify “billions,” without exact figures. Since one is daily and the other weekly, it’s unclear how the AI-related click count compares to overall clicks or what portion of Search traffic comes from AI surfaces. The third group focuses on quality claims. Liz Reid, Google’s head of Search, stated that AI Overviews mainly remove “bounce clicks,” visits where users quickly find a fact and leave. Alphabet's Q2 report puts precise numbers on the overall Search business while Google's claims about clicks to the web stay round and aggregate. Here's what that gap looks like.

Alphabet shared its Q2 earnings this week, showing that Google Search & Other revenue increased by 17% year over year to reach $63.27 billion. For all the details, check out our earnings brief , including how the growth rate has slowed from 19% in Q1, marking the first slowdown after four quarters of accelerating growth.

The numbers also leave out part of the story. Alphabet provides a detailed breakdown of Search business earnings in its securities filing, while Google describes what the web gets back in broad assurances. Both perspectives are now part of every quarter, and the distance between them is the story.

The revenue aspect of Search offers everything you’d hope for from a data source. Alphabet provided clear numbers, comparisons year-over-year, and consistent definitions across quarters, making it straightforward to follow the progress.
The trajectory is checkable: Search & Other growth went from 10% in Q1 2025 to 12%, then 15%, 17%, and reaching 19% in Q1 2026 , before easing back to 17% this quarter.

The spending side got the same precise treatment. Roger Montti covered this , including the capital expenditures that led to negative free cash flow for the quarter.

In July, Nick Fox, senior vice president of Knowledge and Information, noted that Search reached its highest usage on record during a World Cup match. These claims highlight superlatives without providing specific counts. Having more queries does not mean more clicks leaving Google.

The second group involves volume claims. Fox shared in a July LinkedIn post that AI features in Search send billions of clicks to websites weekly. He also mentioned the previous daily figure: “Actually, as we’ve shared before, we continue to send billions of clicks to the web every day through Search.” However, both numbers only specify “billions,” without exact figures. The post also challenged third-party reports of sharp traffic drops, attributing them to flawed methods and isolated cases. coreStoryFacts.text: The thing is, Google, as well as competitors like OpenAI, are still figuring out how to make ads work in AI — both delivering results for advertisers and avoiding alienating the people using their AI tools.

YOY growth for search revenue vs. paid clicks in Q1-3 in 2026 “This is the first major disruption that Google is facing to its core business in decades,” Nate Elliott, an eMarketer principal analyst covering AI and advertising, tells The Verge.
However, Google’s Search revenue growth slowed to 12 percent year over year in the third quarter, down from roughly 17 percent in the previous quarter.
Search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, Google parent Alphabet said in its earnings report last week.
Meanwhile, growth in paid clicks — clicks on ads that generate revenue for Google — slowed from 13 percent to 8 percent.

He added that Google feels good about its trajectory and that its “ad experiments have shown promising results.” It remains unclear whether that reflects a deliberate rollout of ads, as Google says, or a more fundamental problem with advertising in AI search.
An October working paper found that US visits from ChatGPT ads generated 64 percent less revenue for retailers per session than visits from Google Search ads: $0.89 versus $2.45.
What Google’s core Search business looks like increasingly depends on what you ask.
Google’s claim that most AI Mode queries are additional doesn’t tell us how much revenue it could lose from the searches AI Mode replaces.
The working paper measures retailers’ sales rather than platform revenue, and its findings about ChatGPT don’t establish how Google’s own AI ads perform.
AI is changing how people find information — and whether they click on the ads that fund Google’s business.
Google is currently expanding ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode, including internationally and across multiple turns of US AI Mode conversations.
For now, advertisers are still getting results from Google.
Google doesn’t let them separately target that inventory or break out its performance, Taylor says.
The risk is that AI Mode also draws people away from searches that Google monetizes more effectively.
